mainTopic: Is one witness believed that a יבם died? Failed proofs, רבא's refuted קל וחומר, the 'pearl' of ריח הגט, and a new משנה about marrying the wife's sister.
overview: The גמרא asks whether one witness is believed when he says the יבם has died, which would free the woman to marry anyone. The worry is that she dislikes the יבם, so she might accept a weak report without checking. רב ששת tries to prove from a משנה about reversed reports of deaths that one witness is normally believed. The גמרא answers that the משנה can be about two witnesses against two, where the second pair are עדי הזמה. A second proof, from a משנה saying the woman herself is not believed, is rejected: the same reading would wrongly trust one witness for a man, and the line has its own purpose according to רבי עקיבא. רבא then offers a קל וחומר from a married woman, but a scholar shows it fails. The reason the woman is not believed, that she may not check carefully because she dislikes the יבם, applies to one witness too. Next, רב says רבי אלעזר בן מתיא missed a 'pearl' in the פסוק: the rule of ריח הגט, that even an incomplete גט disqualifies a woman from marrying a כהן. Finally, a new משנה begins about a man who married his wife's sister after a false report that his wife had died.

steps.title: The worry: she dislikes the יבם
steps.stepSummary: The end of the reason for doubting a single witness: the woman hates the יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its reason for why one witness might NOT be believed about the יבם's death. The woman dislikes the יבם, so she might be too quick to accept any report that frees her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In general a woman is careful before remarrying on one witness, because if he is wrong she loses a lot. Here that safeguard may be weaker, since she wants to get away from the יבם. So the question of whether one witness is believed stays open, and this sets up רב ששת's attempt to settle it.

keyTerms.meaning: that she hates him (the יבם)
the husband's brother, who would do יבום with the widow

phrases.english: because she hates him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reasoning behind the open question from before this passage.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is one witness believed that the יבם died, even though the woman may be eager to accept it because she hates him?

steps.title: רב ששת quotes a משנה about reversed reports
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the answer is already in a משנה: reports of the order of deaths that were later reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to them: You already learned this. If they told her, "Your husband died, and afterward your son died," and she married, and afterward they told her, "It was the other way around," she must leave her new husband, and the child, both the first and the last, is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת brings a משנה that he thinks answers the question. He quotes the case and its ruling first; he will explain the proof in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband died while their son was still alive, she does not need יבום and may marry anyone. If the son died first and then the husband, she needs יבום and may not marry an outsider. The first report freed her, the second report bound her, and the משנה rules strictly based on the second report.

keyTerms.meaning: you already learned it (in a משנה)
the facts were the other way around
she must leave (her new husband)
a child from a forbidden union, who has a lasting status

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two orders. "Husband died, then son" means she is free and needs no יבום. "Son died, then husband" means she needs יבום. The second report flips her from free to bound.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to them: You learned it.
If they said to her: "Your husband died,
and afterward your son died," and she married,
phrases.notes: Since the son outlived the husband, she would need no יבום, so she was allowed to marry anyone.

phrases.english: and afterward they said to her:
"The matters were reversed" — she must leave,
and the child, first and last, is a mamzer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a משנה to answer the open question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether one witness is believed about the יבם's death.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of "your husband died and afterward your son died" followed by a reversed report.

steps.title: It can't be two witnesses against two
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת asks what the case is. If two witnesses were contradicted by two, why trust the second pair?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say it was two witnesses against two, what makes you rely on these ones? Rely on those ones!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת starts working out what case the משנה must be about. He rules out the idea that two witnesses were contradicted by two others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two witnesses say one thing and two say the opposite, neither pair beats the other. So there would be no reason to follow the second pair and force her to leave her husband. The משנה's strict ruling doesn't fit that case.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? what are the circumstances?
two witnesses against two witnesses
what did you see? (why prefer this side?)

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say it is two and two —
phrases.notes: Two witnesses gave the first report and two others gave the reversed report.

phrases.english: what did you see that you rely on these,
phrases.notes: "These" means the second pair, the ones the משנה follows.

phrases.english: rely on those!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts analyzing the משנה to build the proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the משנה as two witnesses against two.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two pairs cancel each other out, so nothing would justify forcing her out of her marriage.

steps.title: At most it would be a doubtful ממזר
steps.stepSummary: A second problem with two against two: the child would only be a ספק ממזר, not a definite ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also, a ממזר? He is only a possible ממזר!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת adds a second reason why the case can't be two witnesses against two. The משנה calls the child a plain ממזר, which is too strong for a case of doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two pairs cancelling out, we don't know which report is true. So the child would be a ספק ממזר, a doubtful case. The משנה's flat word "ממזר" suggests a case where the second report clearly wins.

keyTerms.meaning: and furthermore
a child whose ממזר status is in doubt

phrases.english: And furthermore, a mamzer?
He is a doubtful mamzer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection to the two-against-two reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two-against-two reading, measured against the משנה's word "ממזר".
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two against two leaves only a doubt, so the child could not be called a definite ממזר.

steps.title: The משנה is precise about who is a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: One might say the משנה was loose with the word ממזר, but the סיפא shows it chooses that word carefully.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the משנה wasn't precise, look at the later part, which teaches: the first child is a ממזר and the last is not a ממזר. Learn from this that it teaches exactly.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת blocks a possible escape. Someone might say "ממזר" here really means "doubtful ממזר," but he shows from the later part of the משנה that it uses the word carefully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא of the same משנה separates a child who is a ממזר from one who is not. A משנה that draws such careful lines would not call a doubtful child a plain ממזר. So the escape fails, and the two-against-two reading stays ruled out.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you would say
he was not precise
the later part of the משנה
exactly, specifically

phrases.english: And if you would say he was not precise —
phrases.notes: "He" is the author of the משנה, and the idea is that he said "ממזר" loosely.

phrases.english: but from the fact that the latter clause teaches:
the first is a mamzer
and the last is not a mamzer,
learn from it that it teaches precisely!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects a possible defense of the two-against-two reading.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the משנה used "ממזר" loosely.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The סיפא shows the משנה separates ממזר from not-ממזר carefully, so its wording is exact.

steps.title: So it must be one witness, who is normally believed
steps.stepSummary: Therefore the first report came from one witness, and only two contradicting witnesses overruled him. Without them, he would be believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it one witness? And the only reason she must leave is that two came and contradicted him. Otherwise, he would be believed!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת finishes his proof. The first report must have come from a single witness, and we can infer that one witness is normally believed about this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two clearly beat one, which explains both the strict ruling and the plain word "ממזר". But the משנה's reason for forcing her out is only the two who contradicted him, so without them the lone witness would have been trusted. Since his report meant she needed no יבום, this shows one witness is believed even here, despite her dislike of the יבם.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, isn't it...?
one (witness)
they contradicted him
he is believed

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת's proof: the משנה's strict wording only works if one witness was contradicted by two, so a lone witness must normally be believed.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not one,
phrases.notes: One witness gave the first report that freed her.

phrases.english: and the reason is that two came and contradicted him,
but if not so — he is believed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With two-against-two ruled out, draws the conclusion of the proof.
steps.raayaObject: One witness is believed that the יבם died.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An inference from the משנה: only the two who contradicted him overruled the single witness.

steps.title: It can be two against two, with עדי הזמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה really is two against two, but the second pair are עדי הזמה, as רב אחא בר מניומי explained elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, it is two against two, and it is like what רב אחא בר מניומי said: it is talking about witnesses of הזמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב ששת's proof. It keeps the two-against-two reading but explains why the second pair wins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With עדי הזמה, the second pair doesn't just tell a different story. They say the first witnesses weren't even there to see it, so the first pair is thrown out completely. Then the second pair clearly wins, the child is a definite ממזר, and nothing is proven about one witness.

keyTerms.meaning: actually, really (keeping the earlier reading)
witnesses who say the first witnesses were somewhere else at the time, which cancels their testimony
an אמורא whose explanation elsewhere is applied here

steps.confusionAlert: עדי הזמה are not just "two more witnesses with another story." They attack the first witnesses themselves, so they beat them. That is why two against two can still give a clear result here.

phrases.english: Actually, it is two and two,
and as Rav Aḥa bar Manyumi said,
with witnesses of hazamah,

steps.triggerLanguage: לָעוֹלָם תְּרֵי וּתְרֵי, וְכִדְאָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב ששת's conclusion by going back to the two-against-two reading.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof that one witness is believed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Two against two was ruled out too quickly. If the second pair are עדי הזמה, they beat the first pair outright.

steps.title: Here too, עדי הזמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא applies רב אחא בר מניומי's idea to our משנה, so the question about one witness stays unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is talking about witnesses of הזמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the עדי הזמה idea directly to our משנה. This closes off רב ששת's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the משנה can be about two against two with עדי הזמה, it says nothing about a single witness. So it cannot settle whether one witness is believed about the יבם's death, and the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: here too

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה can be explained with עדי הזמה, so רב ששת's proof falls away. Whether one witness is believed about the יבם's death is still undecided.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: a proof from a משנה fails if the משנה can fit another case. Here the other case is two against two with עדי הזמה.

phrases.english: Here too, with witnesses of hazamah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the borrowed explanation to our משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Our משנה can be read as dealing with עדי הזמה, so it cannot prove that one witness is believed about the יבם's death.

steps.title: Proof from a משנה that the woman herself is not believed
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי (or רב אחא) brings a משנה: a woman is not believed to say her יבם died. That suggests one witness would be believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי said to רב אשי (some say it was רב אחא): Come and hear. A woman is not believed if she says, 'My יבם died, so I can marry,' or 'My sister died, so I can marry her husband.' The משנה says she is not believed. That suggests one witness would be believed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof for the open question: is one witness believed to say the יבם died?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says that the woman herself is not believed. Since it singles her out, the proof reads it as hinting that an outside witness would be believed. This is a proof from what the משנה leaves unsaid.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the opening for a proof from a source
The brother-in-law who must do יבום or חליצה with his brother's widow
Is believed (said of a woman)
So that I may enter her house: meaning, marry her husband
But: introduces what we learn from the wording

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rav Mordechai said to Rav Ashi,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Acha who said to Rav Ashi:
Come and hear:
A woman is not believed to say
"My יבם died," so that I may marry,
and not "My sister died," so that I may enter her house.
It is she herself who is not believed;
but one witness is believed!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אֵין הָאִשָּׁה נֶאֱמֶנֶת לוֹמַר מֵת יְבָמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 8 left the question about one witness unanswered, so a new proof is tried.
steps.raayaObject: One witness is believed to say the יבם died.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה (later in יבמות) saying the woman herself is not believed, read as implying that a witness is.

steps.title: The end of that same משנה breaks the proof
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה says a man is not believed either. That cannot mean one witness is believed for him, so the inference does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: By your reasoning, look at the end of the משנה: a man is not believed to say, 'My brother died, so I can do יבום with his wife,' or 'My wife died, so I can marry her sister.' Should we say he isn't believed, but one witness would be? With a woman it makes sense, because the Rabbis were lenient so she would not be stuck unable to remarry (עיגונא). But with a man, what reason is there to be lenient?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof by showing that the same style of reading gives a wrong result in the end of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a woman, there is a known reason to accept one witness: the Rabbis did not want her left as an עגונה. A man has no such problem, so there is no reason to trust one witness for him. Since the משנה's wording cannot imply that for the man, it does not imply it for the woman either.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: turning the other side's logic against him
The end part of a משנה
It makes sense with regard to
Being left an עגונה, a woman stuck and unable to remarry
They were lenient

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying one witness is believed for a man. It is saying the opposite: that would make no sense, so the 'she herself is not believed' reading cannot be a real proof.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, say the end of the משנה:
A man is not believed to say
"My brother died," so that I may do יבום with his wife,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מֵתָה אִשְׁתִּי, שֶׁאֶשָּׂא אֶת אֲחוֹתָהּ.
phrases.english: and not "My wife died," so that I may marry her sister.
Is it he himself who is not believed,
but one witness is believed?
It makes sense regarding a woman:
because of the worry that she would be stuck unable to remarry, the Rabbis were lenient with her,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא גַּבֵּי אִישׁ מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר?
phrases.english: but regarding a man, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 9 by applying the same reading to the end of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference from 'she herself is not believed' that one witness is believed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same reading would force a ridiculous result for a man, where there is no עיגונא reason to be lenient.

steps.title: The משנה was needed for רבי עקיבא's view
steps.stepSummary: The משנה about the woman was not hinting about a witness. It was needed to teach something according to רבי עקיבא: she cares about harm to herself more than harm to her children.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה was needed for רבי עקיבא. You might have thought: since רבי עקיבא says a child from a forbidden לאו relationship is a ממזר, a woman would worry about ruining her children and would check carefully, so she should be believed. The משנה teaches us that she worries about ruining herself, but not about ruining her children, so she is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the real reason the משנה says 'the woman is not believed.' This shows the line was never meant to hint that one witness is believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי עקיבא, a יבמה who wrongly marries someone else has a child who is a ממזר. One might think fear of that would make her careful, and therefore believable. The משנה teaches that this fear is not enough to trust her, so the משנה has its own point and no hint about one witness.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed
You might have thought to say
Relationships forbidden by a לאו, a negative command, with no כרת
Ruin or damage
She checks carefully
It teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from 'the woman is not believed' fails, because that line was needed to teach a separate point for רבי עקיבא. The question about one witness for a יבמה is still open.

phrases.english: Rather, when was it needed?
It was needed for רבי עקיבא.
You might have thought to say:
Since רבי עקיבא said
there is a ממזר from relationships forbidden by a לאו,
say that she worries about ruining her children, and so she checks carefully,
so it teaches us
that she worries about ruining herself,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets, but this is still the point being taught.

phrases.english: but she does not worry about ruining her children.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כִּי אִיצְטְרִיךְ — לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אִיצְטְרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 10 showed the inference fails, this step explains what the משנה really teaches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the purpose of the משנה's statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under רבי עקיבא, fear of having ממזר children would make her careful, so she should be believed.
steps.terutzMaskana: She worries about herself, not her children, so she is not believed. The line teaches nothing about one witness.

steps.title: רבא's קל וחומר: one witness is believed for a יבמה
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that one witness is believed about a married woman's husband, which is a כרת prohibition. So surely he is believed for a יבמה, which is only a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: One witness is believed for a יבמה because of a קל וחומר. If you allowed one witness for a prohibition of כרת (a married woman), then for a prohibition that is only a לאו (a יבמה), all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a new source: a logical קל וחומר instead of a proof from wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A married woman who marries someone else breaks a כרת prohibition, which is more serious. Yet one witness who says her husband died is enough to permit her. A יבמה marrying someone else breaks only a לאו, which is lighter, so one witness should surely be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Logic from a stricter case to a lighter one
A prohibition punished by כרת, like a married woman
A prohibition that is a simple negative command, like a יבמה with a stranger
All the more so

phrases.english: רבא said:
One witness is believed for a יבמה
from a קל וחומר.
For a prohibition of כרת you permitted,
phrases.notes: He means a married woman: one witness saying her husband died lets her remarry.

phrases.english: for a prohibition of a לאו, is it not all the more so?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: עֵד אֶחָד נֶאֱמָן בִּיבָמָה מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The proof from the משנה failed, so רבא tries a logical argument instead.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One witness is believed that a יבם died, learned by קל וחומר from a married woman.

steps.title: The woman herself shows the קל וחומר fails
steps.stepSummary: One of the Rabbis points out that the woman herself is believed about her husband (כרת) but not about her יבם (לאו). So the 'lighter' case is not always easier.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the Rabbis said to רבא: The woman herself proves otherwise. For a prohibition of כרת you permitted her, but for a prohibition of a לאו you did not permit her!
steps.whatsHappening: A scholar knocks down רבא's קל וחומר by pointing to a case where the pattern runs the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman is believed on her own word that her husband died, even though that is a כרת issue. Yet by the משנה in step 9, she is not believed that her יבם died, which is only a לאו. Since the lighter case can sometimes be stricter, רבא's 'all the more so' does not hold.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain one of the Rabbis
She herself will prove it: a case that breaks the קל וחומר
You permitted

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's קל וחומר is refuted: the woman's own testimony is accepted for the כרת case but not for the לאו case, so 'lighter' does not mean 'easier to permit' here.

phrases.english: One of the Rabbis said to רבא:
She herself will prove it,
for in a prohibition of כרת you permitted her,
phrases.notes: When she says her own husband died, she is believed and may remarry.

phrases.english: yet in a prohibition of a לאו you did not permit her!
phrases.notes: This is the משנה from step 9: she is not believed that her יבם died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks the קל וחומר of step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's קל וחומר from a married woman to a יבמה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The woman's own testimony is accepted for the stricter כרת case but rejected for the lighter לאו case. That breaks the 'all the more so' logic.

steps.title: Why she is not believed, and why the same worry applies to one witness
steps.stepSummary: The reason a woman is not believed about her יבם is that she may dislike him and not check carefully before remarrying. That same reason applies when one witness testifies, so רבא's קל וחומר fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is she herself not believed? Because sometimes she dislikes him, so she does not check carefully before remarrying. The same is true with one witness: since sometimes she dislikes him, she will not check carefully and will remarry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the woman is not believed about her יבם. It then shows that this very reason also makes one witness unreliable here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One witness is normally trusted because we assume the woman checks the facts carefully before remarrying. With a יבם she may dislike him and want to be free, so we cannot count on her to check. That removes the basis for trusting one witness, and רבא's קל וחומר from the married woman falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: She herself (the woman)
She dislikes (hates) him, meaning the יבם
She checks carefully
She gets married
A single witness

steps.whatToRemember: With a יבם, we cannot assume the woman will check carefully, because she may dislike him. So the usual reason for trusting one witness does not apply, and רבא's proof does not stand.
steps.confusionAlert: The point is not that the witness himself is lying. One witness is only ever trusted because we rely on the woman to double-check, and here we cannot rely on her.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶלָּא אִיהִי מַאי טַעְמָא לָא מְהֵימְנָא,
phrases.english: But rather, she herself, what is the reason she is not believed?
Because since sometimes she dislikes him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the יבם she would otherwise have to marry or get חליצה from.

phrases.english: she does not check carefully and gets married.
With one witness, too:
since sometimes she dislikes him,
she does not check carefully and gets married.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא אִיהִי מַאי טַעְמָא לָא מְהֵימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection begun in step 13 by giving the reason she is not believed and applying it to one witness.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole קל וחומר from a married woman to a יבמה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The trust in one witness depends on the woman checking carefully, and with a יבם she may not check because she dislikes him.

steps.title: רב says רבי אלעזר בן מתיא missed a 'pearl'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's teaching of רבי אלעזר בן מתיא. רב says he could have learned something far more valuable from that פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'This is an exposition taught by רבי אלעזר בן מתיא, etc.' רב יהודה said in the name of רב: רבי אלעזר could have learned a pearl from this פסוק, but he learned a clay shard from it instead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. רב comments that רבי אלעזר בן מתיא used the פסוק for a small lesson when a much bigger one was available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן מתיא used the words 'divorced from her husband' to teach that a גט from a man who is not her husband does not disqualify her. רב calls that lesson a 'clay shard,' something of little value. He says the same words hold a 'pearl,' a more important rule, which the next steps will explain.

keyTerms.meaning: An exposition, a lesson learned from a פסוק
The תנא whose teaching the משנה quoted
A pearl, meaning a valuable lesson
A clay shard, meaning a lesson of little value

phrases.english: This is an exposition taught by
Rabbi Elazar ben Matya, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. He learned from 'divorced from her husband' that a גט from a different man does not disqualify her from a כהן.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לְמִדְרַשׁ בֵּיהּ מַרְגָּנִיתָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar should have expounded a pearl from it,
but he expounded a clay shard from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה מִדְרָשׁ דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן מַתְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: discussion of a different line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק 'divorced from her husband' contains a more important lesson than the one רבי אלעזר בן מתיא drew from it.

steps.title: What is the pearl?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what valuable lesson רב meant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what lesson רב had in mind. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב only said that a better lesson exists, without saying what it is. The גמרא asks for it so the answer can be shown from a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: What?

phrases.english: What is the pearl?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the content of רב's 'pearl' from step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson רב saw in the פסוק

steps.title: The pearl: even a partial גט disqualifies from כהונה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that even a גט that frees a woman only from her own husband disqualifies her from marrying a כהן. This is called ריח הגט.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And a woman divorced from her husband.' Even if she was divorced only from her husband, she is disqualified from marrying a כהן. This is the 'scent of a גט' that disqualifies from כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. Even a weak, incomplete גט that separates her only from her husband is enough to forbid her to a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads 'divorced from her husband' as 'divorced only from her husband.' This is a גט that does not allow her to marry anyone else. Such a גט does not really free her, yet it still makes her forbidden to a כהן. That is the pearl: even a 'scent' of a גט is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
A divorced woman
Disqualified from marrying a כהן
The 'scent' of a גט: an incomplete גט that still has some effect

steps.whatToRemember: ריח הגט: even a גט that does not fully free a woman still disqualifies her from marrying a כהן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known rule of ריח הגט, which comes up in many places in הלכות כהונה.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
"And a woman divorced from her husband"
even if she was divorced only from her husband
phrases.notes: He means the גט only cuts her off from him and does not let her marry anyone else.

phrases.english: she is disqualified from the priesthood.
And this is the scent of a bill of divorce
which disqualifies from the priesthood.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The pearl is that even a גט freeing her only from her husband disqualifies her from a כהן (ריח הגט).

steps.title: New משנה: he married her sister after hearing his wife died
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. A man is told his wife died overseas, he marries her sister, and then his wife returns. The משנה begins to rule that she is permitted to return.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A man's wife went overseas. People came and told him, 'Your wife died,' so he married her sister. Afterward his wife came back. She is permitted to return.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts with a case of a false report of death followed by marriage to the wife's sister. The ruling begins here and continues in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier case of a woman who remarried based on a false report, here the man is the one who remarried, and he married his wife's sister. The משנה starts by saying the original wife may return. Its full ruling and reasons continue past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה: the start of a new משנה
Overseas, far away
Her sister
She is permitted to return

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. 'Permitted to return' means returning to her husband, and the rest of the משנה's ruling comes next.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One whose wife went overseas,
and people came and told him, "Your wife died,"
and he married her sister,
and afterward his wife came back
she is permitted to return

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מִי שֶׁהָלְכָה אִשְׁתּוֹ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה, unrelated to the previous discussion's flow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a man married his wife's sister based on a false report of his wife's death, the original wife is permitted to return to him.
